claim.why_it_matters: Superscript exponents flattened in 8.8.1.3.1.1: '10–999' reads as 10 minus 999, '101000 – 10968' reads as one hundred one thousand minus ten thousand nine hundred sixty-eight; the bounds of the standard intermediate data item magnitude range are wrong as written (the parenthesised E-notation is intact).

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of PDF page 144 (printed page 122), 8.8.1.3.1.1 Precision and allowable magnitude, shows the lower bound as 10 with superscript '-999' and the upper bound as 10 with superscript '1000', an en dash, then 10 with superscript '968'. The transcription (page-144.md lines 15 and 19) reads '10–999' and '101000 – 10968', so the superscript markup is gone and the run-together digits read as different numbers ('10 minus 999', '101000 minus 10968'). Both quotes in the claim match their sources. The parenthesised E-notation equivalents survive and keep the intended values recoverable, but the primary normative expression of the range bounds of a standard intermediate data item is wrong as written. This is a genuine content defect, not scaffolding or wrapping.
